page.title: A clearer view of your days.
page.description: Explore Vietnamese lunar dates, remember special occasions and make time for what matters.
page.seoDescription: Vietnamese solar and lunar calendar, holidays and a time-off calculator. Available in Vietnamese, English, Traditional and Simplified Chinese.

detail.title: Selected day
detail.noEvents: No holiday or observance is listed for this day.
detail.lunarNote: Vietnamese lunar dates stay the same in every language.

upcoming.description: From the month you are viewing
upcoming.empty: No upcoming occasions within the calendar range.

planner.title: Make time for a break
planner.description: Choose a date range to estimate the leave days you need.
planner.note: This estimate follows your choices. It does not automatically include the full Tết break, substitute holidays or swapped workdays. Check your workplace schedule.
planner.invalid: Choose an end date on or after the start date, within 2000–2099.
planner.limit: Calculate up to 366 days at a time.

footer.note: Holiday dates do not include complete annual breaks, substitute holidays or swapped workdays.
footer.privacy: Free to use. No sign-in needed.
footer.madeFor: A little perspective on your days.

newYear.name: New Year's Day
newYear.description: The first day of the Gregorian year.

tet.name: Vietnamese Lunar New Year
tet.description: The first day of the first lunar month. The full Tết break is announced separately each year and by each workplace.

firstFullMoon.name: First Full Moon Festival
firstFullMoon.description: The fifteenth day of the first lunar month, known in Vietnam as Tết Nguyên tiêu.

hungKings.name: Hùng Kings Commemoration
hungKings.description: The tenth day of the third lunar month, commemorating the Hùng Kings.

doanNgo.name: Tết Đoan Ngọ
doanNgo.description: The fifth day of the fifth lunar month, a traditional Vietnamese festival.

vuLan.name: Vu Lan Festival
vuLan.description: The fifteenth day of the seventh lunar month, an occasion to honour parents.

nationalDay.name: Vietnam National Day
nationalDay.description: September 2. The adjoining day off and any workday swaps follow annual announcements.

midAutumn.name: Mid-Autumn Festival
midAutumn.description: The fifteenth day of the eighth lunar month, a time for family reunions and children's celebrations.

kitchenGods.name: Kitchen Gods' Day
kitchenGods.description: The twenty-third day of the twelfth lunar month, marking preparations for the new year.

womensDay.name: International Women's Day
womensDay.description: March 8. An observance, not automatically a day off.

vietnameseWomensDay.name: Vietnamese Women's Day
vietnameseWomensDay.description: October 20. An observance, not automatically a day off.

teachersDay.name: Vietnamese Teachers' Day
teachersDay.description: November 20, an occasion to thank teachers.

christmas.name: Christmas Day
christmas.description: December 25. Not automatically a day off in Vietnam.
